evidence_needed: Timestamped address-to-set moments from at least three creators across the spectacle and roleplay lanes, starting with Neotastic J1r-N1MPuqM (07:14, 09:27) and GrayStillPlays n69RAweU85M (05:13, 18:05)
pole_high: the set is a scene partner: the bridge, the machine, the sea get addressed, blamed and bargained with
pole_low: the set is inert; only beings get motives and direct address
question: Does the creator treat the environment or system itself as a character - addressing it, pleading with it, blaming it, negotiating with it as if it had intentions - or is character work reserved for creatures and people
why: Round 3 put it on camera for both spectacle creators in a single round: Neotastic addresses his bridge by name, pleads with it to fix itself and reads its moods while it bends, and GrayStillPlays argues with items, a named statue and a slow robot fleet. Existing character-work questions (show-023) count creatures and NPCs; in physics sandboxes the most important scene partner is often the structure itself, and an avatar that can talk TO the physics has a whole register the others lack
